primitives.assumptions: Final pitch outcome depends only on its own features and immediate context; no feedback from batter adaptation.

layer2.mapping: Maps concatenated pitch and context vectors to binary classification of in-play vs swing-out using sigmoid activation, forming core probabilistic inference engine in GSI.

reasoning_traces.think:
The framework employs a two-stage pipeline: first, a Transformer-based encoder processes the last six pitches as a 6×7 feature matrix, capturing spatiotemporal dynamics of pitch sequencing. Simultaneously, a 15-dimensional context vector encodes game state and batter history. These are concatenated and passed through dense layers to predict in-play probability. The counterfactual optimization then estimates how altering the final pitch affects season-level stats like K/9, ERA, and opponent slugging. This dual structure enables both micro-decision modeling and macro-statistical impact estimation. Failure modes include overfitting to rare pitch combinations, misalignment between training and test contexts, and incorrect assumptions about pitcher command and batter adaptation. The model assumes linearity in stat estimation and fixed pitcher behavior under counterfactuals.
